subject: Hosted API SLA: measurement alignment & interim bridge plan
messages:
From: Steve Caldwell <steve@brightline.health>
To: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: legal_procurement@brightline.health
Date: 2027-04-25T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Hosted API SLA - how are you measuring p50/p95?

Hi Laura,

Thanks for the demo last week. Legal and our platform team asked me to follow up with a few concrete items so we can advance the SLA review:

- Could you confirm the exact measurement window you intend to use for p50/p95 (rolling 7d/30d, calendar day, etc.)?
- How do you handle regional failover and cross-region routing in the numbers (do you measure per-region or global)?
- Are there standard carveouts for cache warmup, planned maintenance, or upstream provider incidents?
- For the first 90 days post-cutover we'd like an interim bridge plan with explicit targets and monitoring so our product team can validate behavior under peak.

I've attached a sample traffic snapshot so you can see our peak shapes (brightline-traffic-sample.csv). Please loop in anyone on your side who needs to own operational quantification.

Best,
Steve
Steve Caldwell
Head of Platform, Brightline Health
steve@brightline.health

From: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Steve Caldwell <steve@brightline.health>
Cc: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-25T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API SLA - how are you measuring p50/p95?

Steve — thanks for the traffic file and the clear questions. High level answers here, and we can schedule a short sync if you want to walk the examples live.

- Measurement window: our default for Hosted SLA is a 7-day sliding window for p50/p95 with reporting in UTC. For enterprise contracts we can discuss a 30-day baseline for long-term commitments, but the operational SLO uses 7 days to catch regressions faster.
- Regional vs global: we measure at the regional endpoint level (us-west/us-east/eu) and report both per-region and a global aggregated view. The SLA commitment will call out the region-specific figures that matter for your production region.
- Carveouts: standard carveouts include scheduled maintenance (as pre-announced), provider-wide networking incidents (we surface postmortems), and orchestrator cold-starts during large scheduled capacity changes. Cache warmup/cold-starts are treated as an operational transient and we include a short warmup carveout in the bridge plan.

Attaching a first-draft SLA (sla-draft-redwood-v1.docx) and a concise summary below that maps to the questions you raised. Ben and Marissa are copied to confirm commercial/credit language.

Proposal summary (initial):
- Interim 90-day bridge: p50 <= 120ms, p95 <= 450ms per-region measured on a 7-day sliding window; escalate to committed 30-day figures after mutual validation.
- Monitoring: shared dashboard + webhook alerts; Redwood will produce a daily digest for the first 30 days.
- Credits: tiered service credits tied to the number of missed windows in a month (details in the doc).

If that aligns with Brightline's expectations we can push a rev to legal and send a DocuSign request.

Thanks,
Laura
Laura Bennett
Head of Customer Success (Platform)
Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>

Date: 2027-04-26T14:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API SLA - how are you measuring p50/p95? (bridge plan draft)

Steve/Laura — quick commercial note and a concrete bridge plan attached (bridge-plan-initial.pdf). I'll keep this short:

- We can commit to an interim plan (90 days) that gives Brightline headroom to validate production traffic and our routing. The operational targets I recommend for the interim are: p50 <= 120ms, p95 <= 450ms, measured per-region on a 7-day sliding window.
- Carveouts: scheduled maintenance windows (72-hour notice), a one-week carveout for initial capacity ramp, and an explicit cold-start carveout for first-time model warms after a major version switch.
- Credits: 5% monthly credit if there are 2 missed windows in a 30-day period; 15% for 3+ missed windows. We'll refine during legal redlines.

Next step: if Brightline accepts these interim figures we'll update the SLA doc and route to DocuSign for signatures, with monitoring links and runbook attached.

—Ben

From: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@brightline.health>

Subject: Re: Hosted API SLA - measurement alignment & interim bridge plan

Thanks — a few technical clarifications from our infra team before we move to legal:

1) Peak window behavior: our busiest 2-hour window has sustained bursts that exceed your typical median traffic by ~6x. How should we expect p95 to behave during those short peaks? Do you apply any burst smoothing or at-least-once routing that would bias numbers?

2) Cache warmup: can you define the warmup period (how many requests/seconds you consider for "warm"). Also, do you include cold-starts from autoscaling events in the same measurement window or mark them separately?

3) Dashboard: please share the specific dashboard and the metrics names (we need to map to our own alerting).

We prefer explicit language in the SLA around how peaks and cold-starts are treated; otherwise our internal SRE will object to signing.

Emily Zhao
Head of Platform Engineering, Brightline Health
emily.zhao@brightline.health

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@brightline.health>, laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-28T13:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API SLA - measurement alignment & interim bridge plan (technical notes)

Emily — good questions. Some technical specifics to include in the SLA appendix and the measurement methodology doc (attached: measurement-methodology.pdf). Below are the key points we propose to codify:

- Peak windows: p95 is measured across the same distribution even during peaks (no smoothing). However, for short-lived bursts we allow a transient carveout policy: if a region observes a spike >5x baseline for under 2 hours that is attributable to customer traffic shaping, we will mark that period for manual review rather than automatic credit triggers. This protects against noisy neighbor events that are not indicative of sustained degradation.

- Cache warmup: we define a warm state as 30 seconds after the first successful request for a given model variant in a calling session, or after 500 tokens served to that model variant, whichever is earlier. Cold-start latencies from autoscaling (new instance boot) are measured but eligible for a 10-minute operational carveout for the very first instance boot after planned capacity changes.

- Measurement names & dashboard:
  - metric: redwood.request.latency.ms (labels: region, model, route, percentile)
  - metric: redwood.request.success_rate (labels: region, model, route)
  - dashboard (sample): https://grafana.redwood.com/d/abc123/brightline-sla-dashboard

I'll add this language to the SLA appendix and circulate a version with explicit examples (sample queries and how we compute the sliding window) so Brightline can validate against your internal alerts.

Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Director, Product (Inference)
